story.kernfrage: Does the Hopfield bound eta >= e^{-(n+1)Delta} on the error rate of kinetic proofreading hold as a universal limit for networks with two bound states, or can topologies other than the linear chain with one proofreading step go below e^{-2Delta}?
story.kernaussage: Among the 88 non-degenerate rule-compliant two-bound-state topologies, the bound eta >= e^{-2Delta} is proven for 50, exactly certified as violated (eta < 1e-4, down to about 1e-12) for 11 via fuel-driven discard edges, and left open for 27, while the linear Hopfield chain obeys eta >= e^{-(n+1)Delta} for all rates.
story.titel: The Hopfield Bound $e^{-2\Delta}$ Holds for 50 of 88 Two-Bound-State Proofreading Networks and Fails for 11
story.keywords: kinetic proofreading, Hopfield bound, error rate, entropy production, Markov networks, exact certificates
